clue.text: Few days demand to be discussed without resistance

definitions.note: adverbial phrase standing for an adjective meaning feeble, lacking resolve

indicators.note: things discussed are spoken out loud, so we go by the sound of the words, not their spelling

parts.note: a week is a span of a few days
to need something is to demand it

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a few days off and wants to talk it over, giving in without a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Said out loud, WEEK NEED is WEAK-KNEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone weak-kneed lacks the courage or resolve to put up any fight, so they give in easily.

clue.text: Christian campaigner's brief desire, previously, to accommodate Roman Catholic separately

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the last letter of the word for desire goes

parts.note: will means desire, as in 'against her will'

indicators.note: to accommodate means to take in, so the word for previously holds the two letters
separately says the two letters go into different places rather than side by side

parts.note: before means previously
R is the abbreviation for Roman
C is the abbreviation for Catholic, as in RC

explanation.surface: A religious activist briefly longed, beforehand, to make room for Catholics one by one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' cuts WILL to WIL. 'to accommodate' and 'separately' put R and C into BEFORE at different points, giving BERFORCE. The 's means is.
explanation.definitionFit: William Wilberforce was the evangelical Christian MP who led the British campaign to abolish the slave trade.

clue.text: Extremely sharp trim after a time in New York (but not now)

explanation.surface: A sharp haircut in New York, once upon a time.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared in September, when New York runs on Eastern Daylight Time, so standard time is 'not now'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acutest is the superlative of acute, meaning sharpest, keenest, or most intense.

clue.text: Knock back a mild Indian dish

explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially ignored' drops the S from SEX CELL, leaving EXCELL before ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to be outstanding, so excelled is the past tense meaning performed brilliantly.

clue.text: Hanging up pants in yard

clue.text: City unexpectedly re-elects independent

parts.note: the first letter of Elon

clue.text: He performed rural violence, i.e. scuffling

clue.text: Closely examine Cambridge's final call about degree

a Bachelor of Arts degree

clue.text: Relocated coaches firing current agent, accepting blunder

clue.text: At the end of the last night, we never see Homeward Bound

clue.text: Space in berth to sway half-heartedly about

clue.text: Too much off depleted capital

parts.note: away means off, as in 'he is off on holiday'

explanation.walkthrough: OTT is British slang for over the top. 'depleted' cuts AWAY to AWA. 'capital' looks like money, but it is a capital city.

clue.text: Short outing to collect tissue that's much appreciated

explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts TOUR to TOU, and 'to collect' puts HANKY inside it, after the T.

clue.text: Danish scientist flipped over one thousand and one shapes

one thing over another covers it, so it goes round it

explanation.definitionFit: Rhombi is the plural of rhombus, a four-sided figure with all sides equal, so they are shapes.

clue.text: Sorry for reflecting on American who went to hell and back

definitions.text: who went to hell and back

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hell and back' sounds like an ordeal, but it is literal: the underworld.

clue.text: Trademark covering this girl's equally skimpy underwear

indicators.note: covering means the abbreviation goes round the pronoun

clue.text: Inspect some cheesy LA nachos on the counter

Member of Parliament

clue.text: Did judge like some paper?
